newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss banks slam latest attacks over Nazi gold.
newsitem.headline: Swiss banks slam latest attacks over Nazi gold.

text.p: Swiss banks lashed back at Jewish critics on Tuesday for keeping up a volley of accusations about Swiss dealings with Nazi Germany but allegedly failing to co-operate with efforts to clear up the World War Two past.

The Swiss Bankers Association, umbrella organisation for over 400 banks, declined to comment on the latest charges that recently declassified U.S. government files showed Swiss commercial backs had bought gold looted by the Nazis.
Association spokeswoman Silvia Matile said Swiss banks could not comment before seeing the documents, which were presented on Monday in New York by the World Jewish Congress (WJC).

Matile said the latest accusations followed a familiar pattern in recent months by WJC leaders, who she said levelled allegations based on newly found documents that were never passed along to investigators in Switzerland.
"We are constantly being presented with new accusations through the media but we have not yet been able to see a single document," Matile told Reuters.

Matile urged the WJC to channel documents to the joint commission of international experts created last May by major Jewish groups and Swiss banks and headed by former U.S. Federal Reserve Board chairman Paul Volcker.
"It would seem natural that all interested parties work together to uncover the truth," she said.
"We have not yet seen a single document. We hear from the media that some documents allegedly exist and we are instantly accused," she said.

The Volcker commission of seven members, including three named by the WJC and the World Jewish Restitution Organisation, is investigating whether Swiss banks have returned all the assets left by Jews killed in the Holocaust to the legal heirs.

The commission will also cooperate with a historical panel due to be approved by parliament next month with a broader brief to lay open the scope of Swiss financial dealings with both Nazi Germany and its victims.

Both the Volcker commission and the government panel will be empowered to lift banking secrecy to probe dormant wartime-era accounts, although these powers will not compromise the confidentiality of accounts held by modern customers.

The latest documents found by WJC researchers say Basle-based institutes Swiss Bank Corp and Basler Handelsbank received gold worth $2 million (about $20 million by 1996 prices) taken from the Netherlands by Nazi German occupiers.

Matile also angrily rejected renewed claims by WJC vice president Kalman Sultanik that a Swiss banking ombudsman who has been handling claims made by Holocaust survivors or their relatives was engaging in a cruel hoax.
"Ombudsmann Haeni and his team have been working very hard since being given this mission at the start of this year. To talk about a 'cruel hoax' in this connection is shameless," Matile said.

Haeni has scheduled a news conference for later on Tuesday to present the latest status of the search for any dormant accounts that might have been held by Holocaust victims and that have escaped two previous sweeps for such funds.
